Under it all runs the scene life: 26 entries, of which the shore waves and the drifting cloud shadows are built so far; birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and one rain shower are planned.

The banner keeps the same time. The floor moves one grid line per beat (0.75 s at 80 BPM), a new slit starts down the sun on every bar (3 s), her head and the shark's nod once a beat, and the whole story is twelve bars long. It would all be on the beat, if images could make a sound. Source: [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py).

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THE SUN IS HELD UP</b>: the banner, taken apart</summary>

The genre's sun is always setting. This one cannot: the project has a rule that it is always daytime. So it does the next best thing. Six dark slits slide down the lower part of it, one starting every bar, each growing from nothing to about ten pixels thick as it slides out through the base, which is exactly what a setting sun looks like in this style. The disc itself does not move a pixel. It has been setting since 0:00:00 and it will still be setting at 10:00:00.

The rest, back to front:

- **Sky and clouds.** A deep purple gradient and, where the genre puts low-poly mountains, low-poly cumulus: overlapping puffs, their outline zipped into big triangles and lit from below and from the sun's side, the way sunset clouds are. They float a few pixels clear of the horizon, because clouds do.
- **The sea.** A magenta wireframe floor: a fixed fan of lines to the vanishing point and thirty cross lines that all run the same 22.5-second track toward the viewer, one beat apart, with keyframes picked so every straight step stays within 0.35 px of true perspective. Under the sun, its reflection flickers between two sets of broken bars on the beat.
- **The island.** One palm (a curved, tapering trunk and nine drooping fronds with a fringe of leaflets), a raft that bobs, two rings of foam a bar, and her: flat shapes with a dark outline, a nod on every beat and a sip of iced coffee twice a loop.
- **The story.** Twelve bars, 36 seconds. A shark in headphones crosses and nods with her. At 0:12 she turns round and walks out over the water to the vanishing point, stepping twice a beat and shrinking as she goes. The hydrofoil crosses while she is away, and he throws a shaka at the palm, wrist going twice a beat. At 0:22.5 she reappears at the vanishing point and walks back with a fresh one. In the video, when he comes by, she jumps up, runs over and waves, and he waves back. The banner is the only place she has missed him.
- **The word.** Eight heavy, rounded-square capitals drawn as thick stroked centrelines, skewed 13 degrees, filled with a chrome gradient that has one hard stop for the horizon, then outlined, extruded seven steps down and to the right, and glowed with wider, fainter copies. The shine is a soft white bar masked to the letter faces.
- **The brush lettering.** *golden hours* is a spline through hand-placed points, swept by a broad nib held at 38 degrees, so the strokes go thick and thin like a brush, then given a dark backing, a neon glow and a dark drop shadow. It flickers on once when the page loads.

No text elements, no fonts and no filters: every glow is a wider, fainter copy of the same line. One 106 KB SVG with CSS keyframes, regenerated by a dependency-free Node generator. With reduced motion set, it holds a complete frame: her by the palm with the coffee, the shark mid-sea, every word drawn.

</details>

<p align="center">
  <b>キャストアウェイ</b> &nbsp;·&nbsp; ずっと、昼。 &nbsp;·&nbsp; <i>daytime, all the way through</i><br>
  <sub>Short Shadow Records SSR-1992 &nbsp;·&nbsp; one island, one palm, ten hours &nbsp;·&nbsp; side B is also noon</sub>
</p>

**Castaway** (working title) is a ten-hour lo-fi video for YouTube, and this is its sleeve. A young woman sits alone on a very small island with one tall palm and a raft, nodding to the music on her headphones. Every so often, something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back to her feet. A drone lowers a parcel, and the parcel is more headphones. A shark surfaces in headphones of its own and nods along. Then she goes back to nodding, and it is still daytime, because it is always daytime: the video has no night in it, by design.

It is an unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of *Johnny Castaway*, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, repainted as a sunny, hand-painted coastal scene: 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps. More than 90 activities take their turn, most of them on four timers and the rest as follow-ups. Every one starts on the next bar of the music, and every sound is synthesized from code.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>Liner notes</b>: the sound, made entirely from code</summary>

<br>

Every sound in Castaway is synthesized by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no stock loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far, and growing.

- **The theme**: a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, played by electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The crackle is synthesized too. This sleeve has never been near a needle.
- **The ocean**: its own seamless 60-second loop, under everything.
- **Mastering**: the mix sits at -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and levels can be set for the master and for each routine.
- **Reviews**: none yet. Nobody has listened to it. The sleeve is ready before the record, which is how a lot of records go.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>Pressing notes</b>: how the record is cut</summary>

<br>

The renderer is a web page with a live preview. Run `python tools/serve.py`, open http://127.0.0.1:8765/, and it exports a frame-exact, YouTube-ready MP4: the browser encodes the picture as H.264 with WebCodecs (68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), then the server mixes the sound and joins the two. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. The page itself is [web/index.html](web/index.html).

`python tools/render_demo.py --dev` renders a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display, using the older Python reference renderer. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the house style for motion: the needle drops, it does not glide. The label on the record gives its tempo, 80 BPM, in the place where a real label gives its speed.

</details>

| --- | --- | --- |
| キャストアウェイ | kyasuto-awei | Castaway, in katakana |

| 定価 10:00:00 | teika | List price: ten hours, payable in time |
| SSR-1992 | | Catalogue number, after the default seed |

Short Shadow Records is invented, and named for noon, when shadows are shortest. The sleeve is an original drawing in the manner of early-1980s Japanese city pop LP art: no painting was traced and no real label, artist or sleeve is being imitated.

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A 10-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens.<br>
  This is normal. No action is required.</b><br>
  <sub>working title &middot; unofficial, inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i> &middot; 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps &middot; always daytime</sub>
</p>

One young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. She stands on a very small island with her headphones on, nodding to the music, and every so often something happens: a drone delivers a parcel that turns out to be more headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and the crab walks off wearing it, and the bottle she throws out to sea comes straight back. Then nothing happens for a while, which is the main feature.

It is built like the 10-hour lo-fi streams: one fixed shot, and **more than 90 activities** in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml), on four timers plus chained follow-ups. Each one waits for the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

**Run it**, then open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a> for the live preview and the export to a YouTube-ready MP4:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
```

<p><sub>The desktop in the banner is a drawing, but the clock under the preview really counts: it starts at 2:47:03 when the page opens and wraps at 10:00:00, which is how long a run lasts. Please do not restart your computer.</sub></p>

```text
│  rare          every 30 to 60 minutes       about 13                     │
│  super rare    every 3 to 6 hours           about 2, never over 3        │
│  chained       when another task says so    about 20 follow-ups          │
│                                                                          │
│  Start at .... the next bar of the music (one bar is 3 seconds)          │
│  Run for ..... 10:00:00                 Seed ...... 1992                 │
│  Busy ........ about a third of the time. Idle: the rest of it.          │
│                                                                          │
│  [x] Let lanes overlap (a ship may pass while she is busy)               │
│  [x] Run only in daytime                                                 │
│  [ ] Stop the task if it runs for more than 10 hours                     │
│                                                                          │
│                                [   OK   ]  [ Cancel ]  [ Apply ]         │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Counts are medians of 200 simulated 10-hour runs, from the header of [`activities.toml`](activities.toml). Same seed, same schedule, event for event. Lanes are why things can overlap: she has one, and the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore and the kumara patch each have their own. [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py) validates the file and simulates a run.

</details>

The server mixes the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm packages.
- [`python tools/schedule.py`](tools/schedule.py): validates the schedule and simulates a 10-hour run.

- [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): where every sound comes from.

Hard cuts and stepped movement are the motion defaults. The working notes are in [`MUSING.md`](MUSING.md).

<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours on a very small island. Something will happen. Please wait.</b><br>
  <sub>working title &middot; an unofficial remake inspired by the 1992 screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i> &middot; 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps &middot; always daytime</sub>
</p>

A lo-fi video in the spirit of the 10-hour streams and of a classic desert-island screensaver: one young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a lot of time. She sits in the shade with her headphones on and nods to the music. Every few minutes the schedule gives her something small to do, and now and then it pulls something off the Gags menu. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A drone delivers a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A shark in headphones nods along. A coconut lands on a hermit crab, and the crab walks off wearing it. Then she goes back to waiting, which is most of the video, on purpose. Every item on that menu is ready to go except one: **Get Rescued** is greyed out.

**More than 90 activities** live in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml): most of them on four timers, from every 2 to 5 minutes to every 3 to 6 hours, the rest set off by another activity. Every one of them waits for the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), so the gags land on the beat. **Every sound is synthesized from code** by [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): more than 150 files, no samples, no borrowed loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies.

**Run it**, then open <a href="http://127.0.0.1:8765/">http://127.0.0.1:8765/</a> for the live preview and the export to a YouTube-ready MP4:

```sh
python tools/serve.py
```

<p><sub>The banner is only a picture of a computer, so you can stop waiting for it. She won't.</sub></p>

<details>
<summary><b>Gags</b>: the whole menu, pulled down</summary>

- **Message in a Bottle.** She throws it out to sea and it washes straight back. Much later, a different bottle brings a reply.
- **Delivery Drone.** It lowers a parcel and leaves. Inside: another pair of headphones.
- **Sea Turtle Visit.** It swims in, crawls up beside her, and they both doze off.
- **Shark in Headphones.** A fin circles the island; the shark surfaces and nods to the beat.
- **Crab Gets a New Shell.** A coconut drops on a hermit crab. The crab walks off wearing it.
- **Stray Cat Visit.** A grey tabby with a white chest drifts in on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. It comes back another time.
- **Signal Hunt.** One bar of signal, found at the top of the palm.
- **Tour Boat.** A boatful of selfie-takers, with her in the background of every picture.
- **Hydrofoil.** A bro on an electric hydrofoil carves in close, waves a shaka and carves off.
- **Leave Any Time.** She walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee.
- **Bushcraft.** Fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing.
- **Kumara.** She plants one, and it grows over the course of the video.
- **The Everyday.** Coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue, and a sandcastle that the tide takes.
- ~~Get Rescued~~ *(greyed out)*

</details>

The renderer is a plain web page, [`web/index.html`](web/index.html): ES modules, no build step, no npm packages. It exports frame-exact video in the browser (WebCodecs H.264, 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome), and the server mixes in the sound and joins the two into an MP4. Hard cuts and stepped movement are the house style, which is also how this banner moves.

An unofficial remake inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of the 1992 screensaver *Johnny Castaway*, which belongs to its owners. The banner is drawn in the manner of the black-and-white desktops of the late 1980s and early 1990s; its fonts, icons, palm, sea, shark, crab and castaway are all drawn from scratch by a small script, and nothing in it is copied from a real system.
